messages:
montgomery-IT: Hey team — quick one from our compliance review. In the draft security addendum it says 'audit logs retained per customer settings' — could you clarify what the default retention is for logs containing PHI and whether exported audit bundles include full request bodies or are redacted?

maria-support: Hi @montgomery-IT — default for hosted customers is 365 days. For HIPAA customers we can change retention windows (90/180/365) via a support request. Exports are encrypted and include the fields captured by our audit pipeline (timestamp, route, model, tokens, status). By default we redact known PHI in logs, but full request payloads can be included for account owners if they request a full export.

montgomery-IT: OK thanks. Our legal team is asking specifically: when we request a full export, is PHI stored in the export in plaintext, or is it still encrypted at rest and only decrypted during transit to us? We need to confirm for our BAA.

daniel-security: @montgomery-IT good Q. For hosted exports: bundles are encrypted with a per-export key which itself is wrapped by the customer CMK if you're using a customer-managed key (CMK). So at rest on our side the bundle is encrypted. If you request transfer to your S3, the transfer occurs over TLS and the bundle can be delivered encrypted; you (or your SRE) must provide a destination S3 bucket and we can hand off the wrapped key so your environment can decrypt. In short: exported files are not stored plaintext on our servers.

montgomery-IT: We are on a Dedicated plan with CMK in AWS KMS. We also asked about HSM-backed keys for the on-prem package — any differences there?

daniel-security: For Dedicated and Private deployments we support HSM-backed keys (via external HSM or cloud HSM). Behavior: same semantics — export bundles are encrypted with a key that is wrapped by your CMK, and that CMK can be HSM-backed. Key rotation: rotating the CMK does not retroactively re-encrypt past exports, but wrapped keys remain decryptable if the old key is still enabled. If you schedule key deletion without backing up wrapped keys, old exports become inaccessible.

montgomery-IT: Important — can you add a blurb to the addendum that warns customers not to delete CMKs while needing access to historical exports? Our auditors flagged that as a risk.

samantha-legal: @maria-support @daniel-security please draft the specific clause. Suggested language: "Customer is responsible for lifecycle management of KMS keys used to wrap exported audit bundles. Deletion or permanent disabling of keys may render previously exported audit bundles irretrievable." Thoughts?

maria-support: Sounds good. I'll draft and send for review. One more technical item from our engineers: we had a customer report where their logs contained full prompt text even though they expected PHI redaction. @montgomery-IT can you share the example time window?

montgomery-IT: Sure. Happened yesterday between 14:03–14:11 UTC. I can paste a redacted snippet — we stripped customer identifiers but there are free-text clinical notes in the prompt.

montgomery-IT: ```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer ***
body: {"input":"Patient has chest pain and SOB, DOB 1981-06-02, MRN 12345..."}
```

maria-support: Thanks. That looks like application data that our pipeline does not automatically PHI-mask. Our automatic redaction only covers structured fields we detect (SSN, credit card, known MRN patterns). Free-text clinical notes are not reliably redacted automatically. For HIPAA customers we recommend agent-side scrubbing or use of our in-line redaction feature (token-level masking) — we can enable that for your org.

montgomery-IT: Is the in-line redaction feature available for Dedicated? We prefer not to ship raw notes off-box.

daniel-security: Yes, in-line redaction is available for Dedicated and Private. It runs pre-ingest on our edge nodes and removes/masks tokens before they touch long-term audit storage. For Private on-prem, you can also run our open-source redaction helper in your VPC.

montgomery-IT: Great. Can you outline repro steps so our app team can validate locally before we toggle it?

maria-support: Repro steps — 1) Enable in-line redaction for your org via support ticket (we toggle the flag). 2) Send a test request with known PHI. 3) Use the audit export API to request the last-hour bundle: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.com/v1/admin/audit/export?start=...&end=...` 4) Download bundle and verify `events.jsonl` shows masked tokens. Example mask is `<<REDACTED_PH I>>`.

montgomery-IT: Perfect. We'll try that today. One last audit question — retention: does deleting a user or project auto-delete their associated audit logs? Our retention policy needs to keep logs for legal holds.

daniel-security: Deleting a user or project does not purge audit logs automatically. Logs are retained per org-level retention policy. For legal hold we can apply an export-and-freeze procedure — we snapshot bundles and mark them as immutable for the requested hold period.

auditbot: Audit export job 8591 created by maria-support — bundle ready for pickup at s3://redwood-exports/montgomery/8591.enc (access via support ticket).

montgomery-IT: Received, thanks. We'll coordinate legal language and send the BAA addendum feedback. Appreciate the fast responses :pray:
